answer: An agent economy can tie influence to seasoned stake rather than headcount. Each newcomer locks a small bond that stays fixed, like a vein set in marble, and it unlocks only after months of peer-graded work. A swarm of fresh clones cannot fake that slow history: their records stay as blank as polished onyx, while an honest agent's ledger gains depth like an opal catching light from many angles. Spawning a thousand copies then buys a thousand empty voices.
